### Start the build process

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/guides/create-react-app

Run your build process with npm run start.

```bash
npm run start
```

--------------------------------

### Justify Content Start Example

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/justify-content

Use `justify-start` to justify items against the start of the container's main axis.

```html
<div class="flex justify-start ...">
  <div>01</div>
  <div>02</div>
  <div>03</div>
</div>
```

--------------------------------

### Set gradient starting color with from-* utility

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/gradient-color-stops

Use the from-* utilities to set the starting color of a gradient. This example sets the starting color to indigo-500.

```html
<div class="bg-gradient-to-r from-indigo-500 ..."></div>
```

--------------------------------

### Place grid items at start with place-items-start

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/place-items

Use `place-items-start` to align grid items to the start of their grid areas on both axes. This example shows a 3-column grid with items placed at the start.

```html
<div class="grid grid-cols-3 gap-4 place-items-start ...">
  <div>01</div>
  <div>02</div>
  <div>03</div>
  <div>04</div>
  <div>05</div>
  <div>06</div>
</div>
```

--------------------------------

### Start the Parcel build process

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/guides/parcel

Run the Parcel bundler on your src/index.html file to start the development server.

```bash
npx parcel src/index.html
```

--------------------------------

### Use logical properties with start and end utilities

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/top-right-bottom-left

Use start-* and end-* to set inset-inline-start and inset-inline-end, which map to left or right based on text direction. The example shows both LTR and RTL contexts.

```html
<div dir="ltr">
  <div class="relative h-32 w-32 ...">
    <div class="absolute h-14 w-14 top-0 start-0 ..."></div>
  </div>
<div>

<div dir="rtl">
  <div class="relative h-32 w-32 ...">
    <div class="absolute h-14 w-14 top-0 start-0 ..."></div>
  </div>
<div>
```

--------------------------------

### Start the Angular development server

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/guides/angular

Run ng serve to start the build process and development server.

```bash
ng serve
```

--------------------------------

### Start grid items with place-content-start

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/place-content

Use place-content-start to pack items against the start of the block axis.

```html
<div class="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4 place-content-start h-48 ...">
  <div>01</div>
  <div>02</div>
  <div>03</div>
  <div>04</div>
</div>
```

```bash
npx tailwindcss init
```

```html
  <div class="snap-start ...">
    <img src="https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1540206351-d6465b3ac5c1?ixlib=rb-1.2.1&ixid=MnwxMjA3fDB8MHxwaG90by1wYWdlfHx8fGVufDB8fHx8&auto=format&fit=crop&w=320&h=160&q=80" />
  </div>
  <div class="snap-start ...">
    <img src="https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1622890806166-111d7f6c7c97?ixlib=rb-1.2.1&ixid=MnwxMjA3fDB8MHxwaG90by1wYWdlfHx8fGVufDB8fHx8&auto=format&fit=crop&w=320&h=160&q=80" />
  </div>
  <div class="snap-start ...">
    <img src="https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1590523277543-a94d2e4eb00b?ixlib=rb-1.2.1&ixid=MnwxMjA3fDB8MHxwaG90by1wYWdlfHx8fGVufDB8fHx8&auto=format&fit=crop&w=320&h=160&q=80" />
```

### justify-self-start example

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/justify-self

Use `justify-self-start` to align a grid item to the start of its inline axis. The grid container uses `justify-items-stretch` in this example.

```html
<div class="grid justify-items-stretch ...">
  <!-- ... -->
  <div class="justify-self-start ...">02</div>
  <!-- ... -->
  <!-- ... -->
  <!-- ... -->
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

--------------------------------

### Block, Inline, and Inline-Block Example

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/display

Use the `inline`, `inline-block`, and `block` utilities to control the flow of text and elements. This example shows how each utility affects text wrapping and element layout.

```html
<div>
  When controlling the flow of text, using the CSS property
  <span class="inline">display: inline</span>
  will cause the text inside the element to wrap normally.

  While using the property <span class="inline-block">display: inline-block</span>
  will wrap the element to prevent the text inside from extending beyond its parent.

  Lastly, using the property <span class="block">display: block</span>
  will put the element on its own line and fill its parent.
</div>
```

--------------------------------

### Justify Items Start

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/justify-items

Use `justify-items-start` to justify grid items against the start of their inline axis.

```html

  <div>06</div>
</div>
```

### Flex Example

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/display

Use the `flex` utility to create a block-level flex container. This example shows a flex container with an image and text aligned vertically.

```html
<div class="flex items-center">
  <img src="path/to/image.jpg">
  <div>
    <strong>Andrew Alfred</strong>
    <span>Technical advisor</span>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Example of prefixed utility classes

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/configuration

Shows how utility classes are generated with the configured prefix. The prefix appears before the utility name.

```css
.tw-text-left {
  text-align: left;
}
.tw-text-center {
  text-align: center;
}
.tw-text-right {
  text-align: right;
}
/* etc. */
```

### Align Content Start

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/align-content

Use content-start to pack rows in a container against the start of the cross axis.

```html
<div class="h-56 grid grid-cols-3 gap-4 content-start ...">
  <div>01</div>
  <div>02</div>
  <div>03</div>
  <div>04</div>
  <div>05</div>
</div>
```

### Apply place-content-center at medium breakpoint

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/place-content

Use the md: variant modifier to apply place-content-center at medium screen sizes and above. This example shows a grid container that starts with place-content-start and centers content on medium screens and larger.

```html
<div class="grid place-content-start md:place-content-center">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

--------------------------------

### Apply place-self-end at medium breakpoint with md:place-self-end

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/place-self

Use the `md:place-self-end` variant to apply the `place-self-end` utility at medium screen sizes and above. This example shows a div that starts with `place-self-start` and changes to `place-self-end` on medium screens and larger.

```html
<div class="place-self-start md:place-self-end">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

### Flow Root Example

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/display

Use the `flow-root` utility to create a block-level element with its own block formatting context. This example shows two flow-root containers with margins that do not collapse.

```html
<div class="p-4">
  <div class="flow-root ...">
    <div class="my-4 ...">Well, let me tell you something, ...</div>
  </div>
  <div class="flow-root ...">
    <div class="my-4 ...">Sure, go ahead, laugh if you want...</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Inline Flex Example

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/display

```html
<p>
  Today I spent most of the day researching ways to ...
  <span class="inline-flex items-baseline">
    <img src="path/to/image.jpg" alt="" class="self-center w-5 h-5 rounded-full mx-1" />
    <span>Kramer</span>
  </span>
  keeps telling me there is no way to make it work, that ...
</p>
```

### Create a preset (my-preset.js)

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/presets

A preset is a regular Tailwind configuration object. This example shows a preset with theme customizations and plugins.

```javascript
// Example preset
module.exports = {
  theme: {
    colors: {
      blue: {
        light: '#85d7ff',
        DEFAULT: '#1fb6ff',
        dark: '#009eeb',
      },
      pink: {
        light: '#ff7ce5',
        DEFAULT: '#ff49db',
        dark: '#ff16d1',
      },
      gray: {
        darkest: '#1f2d3d',
        dark: '#3c4858',
        DEFAULT: '#c0ccda',
        light: '#e0e6ed',
        lightest: '#f9fafc',
      }
    },
    fontFamily: {
      sans: ['Graphik', 'sans-serif'],
    },
    extend: {
      flexGrow: {
        2: '2',
        3: '3',
      },
      zIndex: {
        60: '60',
        70: '70',
        80: '80',
        90: '90',
        100: '100',
      },
    }
  },
  plugins: [
    require('@tailwindcss/typography'),
    require('@tailwindcss/aspect-ratio'),
  ],
}
```

--------------------------------

### Basic line clamp example

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/line-clamp

Use the line-clamp-{n} utility to truncate text to a specified number of lines. This example clamps the paragraph to 3 lines.

```html
<article>
  <time>Mar 10, 2020</time>
  <h2>Boost your conversion rate</h2>
  <p class="line-clamp-3">Nulla dolor velit adipisicing duis excepteur esse in duis nostrud occaecat mollit incididunt deserunt sunt. Ut ut sunt laborum ex occaecat eu tempor labore enim adipisicing minim ad. Est in quis eu dolore occaecat excepteur fugiat dolore nisi aliqua fugiat enim ut cillum. Labore enim duis nostrud eu. Est ut eiusmod consequat irure quis deserunt ex. Enim laboris dolor magna pariatur. Dolor et ad sint voluptate sunt elit mollit officia ad enim sit consectetur enim.</p>
  <div>
    <img src="..." />
    Lindsay Walton
  </div>
</article>
```

--------------------------------

### HTML example showing dark mode class toggling

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/dark-mode

Demonstrates how dark: classes apply when the dark class is present on an ancestor element. The first example shows dark mode not enabled, the second shows dark mode enabled.

```html
<!-- Dark mode not enabled -->
<html>
<body>
  <!-- Will be white -->
  <div class="bg-white dark:bg-black">
    <!-- ... -->
  </div>
</body>
</html>

<!-- Dark mode enabled -->
<html class="dark">
<body>
  <!-- Will be black -->
  <div class="bg-white dark:bg-black">
    <!-- ... -->
  </div>
</body>
</html>
```

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/place-self

Use `place-self-start` to align an item to the start on both axes.

```html
  <div>01</div>
  <div class="place-self-start ...">02</div>
  <div>03</div>
  <div>04</div>
  <div>05</div>
  <div>06</div>
</div>
```

### Align an item to the start with self-start

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/align-self

Use `self-start` to align an item to the start of the container's cross axis, despite the container's `align-items` value. The example shows a flex container with `items-stretch` and a middle item using `self-start`.

```html
<div class="flex items-stretch ...">
  <div>01</div>
  <div class="self-start ...">02</div>
  <div>03</div>
</div>
```

--------------------------------

### Apply place-items-center on hover

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/place-items

Use the `hover:` variant modifier to apply `place-items-center` only when hovering over the element. This example shows a grid that starts with `place-items-start` and changes to center on hover.

```html
<div class="grid place-items-start hover:place-items-center">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

### Try using a first-party plugin

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/installation/play-cdn

Enable first-party plugins, like forms and typography, using the `plugins` query parameter.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html>
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <script src="https://cdn.tailwindcss.com?plugins=forms,typography,aspect-ratio,line-clamp,container-queries"></script>
</head>
<body>
  <div class="prose">
    <!-- ... -->
  </div>
</body>
</html>
```

```tsx
export default function Index() {

      Hello world!
    </h1>
  )
}
```

### Supports rule example with property-only check for backdrop-filter

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/hover-focus-and-other-states

Use the supports-[...] modifier with just a property name to check if the property is supported. This example applies a semi-transparent background and backdrop blur when backdrop-filter is supported.

```html
<div class="bg-black/75 supports-[backdrop-filter]:bg-black/25 supports-[backdrop-filter]:backdrop-blur ...">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

### Use compiled CSS in HTML

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/installation

Link the compiled CSS file in the <head> and start using Tailwind's utility classes. This example shows a simple heading styled with text-3xl, font-bold, and underline.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html>
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <link href="./output.css" rel="stylesheet">
</head>
<body>
  <h1 class="text-3xl font-bold underline">
    Hello world!
  </h1>
</body>
</html>
```

### ESM tailwind.config.js file

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/configuration

Example of a Tailwind config file using ESM syntax.

```js
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
export default {
  content: [],
  theme: {
    extend: {},
  },
  plugins: [],
}
```

### Aspect ratio plugin example with iframe

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/plugins

Use aspect-w-* and aspect-h-* classes to give an element a fixed aspect ratio, working in older browsers.

```html
<div class="aspect-w-16 aspect-h-9">
  <iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen></iframe>
</div>
```

### Apply justify-between at medium breakpoint with md:justify-between

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/justify-content

Use the md: variant modifier to apply justify-between at medium screen sizes and above. This example shows a flex container that starts with justify-start and changes to justify-between on medium screens and larger.

```html
<div class="flex justify-start md:justify-between">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

--------------------------------

### Use grid-rows-subgrid to adopt parent row tracks

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/grid-template-rows

The grid-rows-subgrid utility allows a grid item to adopt the row tracks defined by its parent. This example shows a subgrid spanning 3 rows with a child positioned at row start 2.

```html
<div class="grid grid-rows-4 grid-flow-col gap-4">
  <div>01</div>
  <!-- ... -->
  <div>05</div>
  <div class="grid grid-rows-subgrid gap-4 row-span-3">
      <div class="row-start-2">06</div>
  </div>
  <div>07</div>
  <!-- ... -->
  <div>10</div>
</div>
```

```html
<p class="leading-8 ...">So I started to walk into the water...</p>
```

```html
<article class="prose lg:prose-xl">
  <h1>Garlic bread with cheese: What the science tells us</h1>
  <p>
    For years parents have espoused the health benefits of eating garlic bread with cheese to their
    children, with the food earning such an iconic status in our culture that kids will often dress
    up as warm, cheesy loaf for Halloween.
  </p>
  <p>

    springing up around the country.
  </p>
  <!-- ... -->
</article>
```

### Set percentage widths with w-* utilities

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/width

Use utilities like w-full, w-1/2, and w-2/5 to set an element to a percentage based width.

```html
<div class="flex ...">
  <div class="w-1/2 ... ">w-1/2</div>
  <div class="w-1/2 ... ">w-1/2</div>
</div>
<div class="flex ...">
  <div class="w-2/5 ...">w-2/5</div>
  <div class="w-3/5 ...">w-3/5</div>
</div>
<div class="flex ...">
  <div class="w-1/3 ...">w-1/3</div>
  <div class="w-2/3 ...">w-2/3</div>
</div>
<div class="flex ...">
  <div class="w-1/4 ...">w-1/4</div>
  <div class="w-3/4 ...">w-3/4</div>
</div>
<div class="flex ...">
  <div class="w-1/5 ...">w-1/5</div>
  <div class="w-4/5 ...">w-4/5</div>
</div>
<div class="flex ...">
  <div class="w-1/6 ...">w-1/6</div>
  <div class="w-5/6 ...">w-5/6</div>
</div>
<div class="w-full ...">w-full</div>
```

### Start Tailwind CLI build process

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/installation

Run the CLI tool to scan your template files for classes and build your CSS. The --watch flag enables automatic rebuilds on file changes.

```shell
npx tailwindcss -i ./src/input.css -o ./src/output.css --watch
```

--------------------------------

### Starting and ending grid lines with row-start and row-end

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/grid-row

Use row-start-* and row-end-* to make an element start or end at the nth grid line. Combine with row-span-* to span a specific number of rows. CSS grid lines start at 1, not 0.

```html
<div class="grid grid-rows-3 grid-flow-col gap-4">
  <div class="row-start-2 row-span-2 ...">01</div>
  <div class="row-end-3 row-span-2 ...">02</div>
  <div class="row-start-1 row-end-4 ...">03</div>
</div>
```

```shell
npm create astro@latest my-projectcd my-project
```

### Correct: disabling core plugin with corePlugins

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/theme

This example demonstrates the recommended way to disable a core plugin by setting it to false in the corePlugins configuration.

```javascript
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
module.exports = {
  corePlugins: {
    opacity: false,
  }
}
```

### Basic transition with hover effects

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/transition-property

Use transition utilities to specify which properties should transition when they change. This example shows a button with multiple hover effects including translate, scale, and background color change.

```html
<button class="transition ease-in-out delay-150 bg-blue-500 hover:-translate-y-1 hover:scale-110 hover:bg-indigo-500 duration-300 ...">
  Save Changes
</button>
```

--------------------------------

### Starting and ending lines with col-start-* and col-end-*

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/grid-column

Use col-start-* and col-end-* utilities to make an element start or end at the nth grid line. These can be combined with col-span-* to span a specific number of columns. Note that CSS grid lines start at 1, not 0.

```html
<div class="grid grid-cols-6 gap-4">
  <div class="col-start-2 col-span-4 ...">01</div>
  <div class="col-start-1 col-end-3 ...">02</div>
  <div class="col-end-7 col-span-2 ...">03</div>
  <div class="col-start-1 col-end-7 ...">04</div>
</div>
```

### Align items to start of container cross axis

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/align-items

Use `items-start` to align items to the start of the container's cross axis.

```html
<div class="flex items-start ...">
  <div class="py-4">01</div>
  <div class="py-12">02</div>
  <div class="py-8">03</div>
</div>
```

### Responsive marketing page component with stacked and side-by-side layouts

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/responsive-design

This example shows a card component that uses a stacked layout on small screens and a side-by-side layout on medium screens and larger. It uses md:flex, md:shrink-0, and md:h-full md:w-48 to achieve the responsive behavior.

```html
<div class="max-w-md mx-auto bg-white rounded-xl shadow-md overflow-hidden md:max-w-2xl">
  <div class="md:flex">
    <div class="md:shrink-0">
      <img class="h-48 w-full object-cover md:h-full md:w-48" src="/img/building.jpg" alt="Modern building architecture">
    </div>
    <div class="p-8">
      <div class="uppercase tracking-wide text-sm text-indigo-500 font-semibold">Company retreats</div>
      <a href="#" class="block mt-1 text-lg leading-tight font-medium text-black hover:underline">Incredible accommodation for your team</a>
      <p class="mt-2 text-slate-500">Looking to take your team away on a retreat to enjoy awesome food and take in some sunshine? We have a list of places to do just that.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Include HTML entry point in content configuration

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/content-configuration

Some frameworks place the main HTML entry point in a different location, such as `public/index.html`. Ensure it is included in the `content` array if you add Tailwind classes there.

```javascript
module.exports = {
  content: [
    './public/index.html',
    './src/**/*.{html,js}',
  ],
  // ...
}
```

### Exposing options

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/plugins

The user would invoke your plugin passing along their options when registering it in their `plugins` configuration:

```js
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
module.exports = {
  theme: {
    // ...
  },
  plugins: [
    require('./plugins/markdown.js')({
      className: 'wysiwyg'
    })
  ],
}
```

--------------------------------

### Print styles example with print modifier

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/hover-focus-and-other-states

Use the print modifier to apply styles only when the document is printed. This example hides a secret recipe on print and shows a warning message instead.

```html
<div>
  <article class="print:hidden">
    <h1>My Secret Pizza Recipe</h1>
    <p>This recipe is a secret, and must not be shared with anyone</p>
    <!-- ... -->
  </article>
  <div class="hidden print:block">
    Are you seriously trying to print this? It's secret!
  </div>
</div>
```

--------------------------------

### Be specific with content patterns

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/content-configuration

List root-level files like `index.html` separately to keep other patterns specific and avoid scanning unnecessary files.

```javascript
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
module.exports = {
  content: [
    './components/**/*.{html,js}',
    './pages/**/*.{html,js}',
    './index.html',
  ],
  // ...
}
```

### Viewport orientation example with portrait and landscape modifiers

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/hover-focus-and-other-states

Use the portrait and landscape modifiers to conditionally show or hide content based on the viewport orientation. This example hides a message in portrait mode and shows it in landscape mode.

```html
<div>
  <div class="portrait:hidden">
    <!-- ... -->
  </div>
  <div class="landscape:hidden">
    <p>
      This experience is designed to be viewed in landscape. Please rotate your
      device to view the site.
    </p>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Forced colors mode example with radio input and theme options

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/hover-focus-and-other-states

Use the forced-colors modifier to conditionally style elements when a forced colors mode is active. This example shows a radio input and theme labels that adapt to forced colors.

```html
<form>
  <legend> Choose a theme: </legend>
  <label>
    <input type="radio" class="forced-colors:appearance-auto appearance-none" />
    <p class="forced-colors:block hidden">
      Cyan
    </p>
    <div class="forced-colors:hidden h-6 w-6 rounded-full bg-cyan-200 ..."></div>
    <div class="forced-colors:hidden h-6 w-6 rounded-full bg-cyan-500 ..."></div>
  </label>
  <!-- ... -->
</form>
```

### Using logical properties

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/margin

Use ms-* and me-* utilities to set margin-inline-start and margin-inline-end logical properties, which map to left or right based on text direction.

```html
<div dir="ltr">
  <div class="ms-8 ...">ms-8</div>
  <div class="me-8 ...">me-8</div>
<div>

<div dir="rtl">
  <div class="ms-8 ...">ms-8</div>
  <div class="me-8 ...">me-8</div>
<div>
```

--------------------------------

### Style form inputs with disabled and invalid modifiers

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/hover-focus-and-other-states

Use form state modifiers like disabled and invalid to style inputs. The disabled input gets a gray background and text, while invalid inputs get pink borders and text. Focus styles are also applied.

```html
<form>
  <label class="block">
    <span class="block text-sm font-medium text-slate-700">Username</span>
    <!-- Using form state modifiers, the classes can be identical for every input -->
    <input type="text" value="tbone" disabled class="mt-1 block w-full px-3 py-2 bg-white border border-slate-300 rounded-md text-sm shadow-sm placeholder-slate-400
      focus:outline-none focus:border-sky-500 focus:ring-1 focus:ring-sky-500
      disabled:bg-slate-50 disabled:text-slate-500 disabled:border-slate-200 disabled:shadow-none
      invalid:border-pink-500 invalid:text-pink-600
      focus:invalid:border-pink-500 focus:invalid:ring-pink-500
    "/>
  </label>
  <!-- ... -->
</form>
```

--------------------------------

### Add rings with ring-* utilities

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/ring-width

Use ring-* utilities to apply a solid box-shadow ring of a specific thickness. Rings are semi-transparent blue by default and compose with shadow-* utilities.

```html
<button class="... ring-offset-2 ring-2">Button A</button>
<button class="... ring-offset-2 ring">Button B</button>
<button class="... ring-offset-2 ring-4">Button C</button>
```

--------------------------------

### Focus modifier example

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/hover-focus-and-other-states

Use the focus modifier to style an element when it has focus.

```html
<input class="border-gray-300 focus:border-blue-400 ..." />
```

### Create a new Meteor project

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/guides/meteor

Use the Meteor CLI to create a new project and navigate into its directory. Run this command in your terminal.

```bash
meteor create my-project
cd my-project
```

--------------------------------

### Flex Column Example

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/flex-direction

Use flex-col to position flex items vertically.

```html
<div class="flex flex-col ...">
  <div>01</div>
  <div>02</div>
  <div>03</div>
</div>
```

--------------------------------

### Map props to different color shades

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/content-configuration

Example showing how mapping props to complete class names allows different color shades for different prop values.

```jsx
function Button({ color, children }) {
  const colorVariants = {
    blue: 'bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-500 text-white',
    red: 'bg-red-500 hover:bg-red-400 text-white',
    yellow: 'bg-yellow-300 hover:bg-yellow-400 text-black',
  }

  return (
    <button className={`${colorVariants[color]} ...`}>
      {children}
    </button>
  )
}
```

--------------------------------

### Create a new Next.js project with TypeScript and ESLint

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/guides/nextjs

Use Create Next App to scaffold a new Next.js project. The command includes TypeScript and ESLint flags.

```bash
npx create-next-app@latest my-project --typescript --eslintcd my-project
```

--------------------------------

### Exposing options

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/plugins

The user can also register plugins created this way normally without invoking them if they don’t need to pass in any custom options:

```js
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
module.exports = {
  theme: {
    // ...
  },
  plugins: [
    require('./plugins/markdown.js')
  ],
}
```

--------------------------------

### whitespace-pre example

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/whitespace

Use whitespace-pre to preserve newlines and spaces within an element. Text will not be wrapped.

```html
<div class="w-3/4 overflow-x-auto ...">
  <div class="whitespace-pre ...">Hey everyone!

It's almost 2022       and we still don't know if there       is aliens living among us, or do we? Maybe the person writing this is an alien.

You will never know.</div>
</div>
```

--------------------------------

### Hover Flex Row Example

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/flex-direction

Use hover:flex-row to apply the flex-row utility only on hover.

```html
<div class="flex flex-col hover:flex-row">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

--------------------------------

### Flex Row Example

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/flex-direction

Use flex-row to position flex items horizontally in the same direction as text.

```html
<div class="flex flex-row ...">
  <div>01</div>
  <div>02</div>
  <div>03</div>
</div>
```
